MICB 201.title: Introductory Environmental Microbiology
MICB 201.description: Prokaryotic diversity and the impact and applications of bacterial and archaeal metabolic, genetic, and growth processes in environmental contexts.
notes: For students with BIOL 112, CHEM 121 is recommended.

MICB 202.title: Introductory Medical Microbiology and Immunology
MICB 202.description: Introduction to cellular and humoral immune responses, the properties of viruses and the principles of bacterial pathogenesis. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.)
MICB 202.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 112, BIOL 200, BMEG 245, MICB 201, SCIE 001

MICB 203.title: Basic Microbiology Laboratory
MICB 203.description: Procedures and principles associated with isolation, characterization and handling of microorganisms. Intended for students requiring a basic microbiology laboratory course.

MICB 205.title: Fundamental Data Science in Microbiology and Immunology
MICB 205.description: Foundations in data science course that incorporates the use of biological data science tools to perform survey-level analysis of microbiology and immunology datasets.

MICB 211.title: Foundations of Microbiology
MICB 211.description: Prokaryotic diversity and the impact and applications of microbial metabolic, genetic, and growth processes in environmental contexts. Bacteria-human interactions in health and disease, mode of action of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance, virulence factors of bacteria, and host response to infection.
MICB 211.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BIOL_V 112, CHEM_V 121 or (b) one of BIOL_V 200, BMEG_V 245, SCIE_V 001, BIOL_O 200

MICB 212.title: Introductory Immunology & Virology
MICB 212.description: Innate and adaptive immune responses to bacterial and viral pathogens, autoimmunity, allergies and graft rejection; virus structure, replication cycles, pathogenesis and vaccines; data analysis of foundational immunology and virology experiments.
MICB 212.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 112, BIOL 200, BMEG 245, SCIE 001

MICB 301.title: Microbial Ecophysiology
MICB 301.description: Dynamics and control of prokaryotic cellular processes in response to the biotic and abiotic environment including metabolic interactions and metabolic cooperation between microorganisms.
MICB 301.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MICB 211, MICB 201 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203; or (b) BIOT 380

MICB 302.title: Immunology
MICB 302.description: Mechanisms of innate and adaptive immune responses. Hematopoiesis, development of T and B lymphocytes, leukocyte migration, antigen processing/presentation and the major histocompatibility complex, immune responses against pathogens, and diseases associated with aberrant immune responses.

MICB 305.title: Data Science in Microbiology and Immunology Research
MICB 305.description: A team-based data science research experience in microbiology and immunology.

MICB 306.title: Molecular Virology
MICB 306.description: Cellular and molecular virology of select human viral pathogens, emphasizing host–virus interactions and antiviral strategies.
MICB 306.prerequisiteText: a) One of BIOL_V 200, BMEG_V 245, BIOT_V 380 and b) one of MICB_V 212, MICB_V 202

MICB 308.title: Paradigms in Bacterial Pathogenesis
MICB 308.description: Mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis including adherence, invasion, intracellular survival, toxins, host defenses and microbial evasion strategies, antibiotics, and vaccines. Introduction to experimental approaches used to study bacterial pathogens.
MICB 308.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MICB 211, MICB 202 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203; or (b) BIOT 380

MICB 322.title: Molecular Microbiology Laboratory
MICB 322.description: Application of foundational skills to common techniques used in classical and molecular microbiology. Restricted to students in Microbiology and Immunology specializations.

MICB 323.title: Molecular Immunology and Virology Laboratory
MICB 323.description: Genetic manipulations of bacteria, introductory immunological and virological procedures, tissue culture. Restricted to students in Microbiology and Immunology specializations.

MICB 325.title: Analysis of Microbial Genes and Genomes
MICB 325.description: Genetic, molecular biological and bioinformatic approaches for the analysis of microbial genomes, gene structure-function and gene expression with emphasis on bacteria.

MICB 353.title: Food Microbiology Laboratory
MICB 353.description: Procedures and principles associated with isolation, enumeration, characterization and handling of microorganisms. Restricted to students registered in the Food Science program.
MICB 353.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 112, MICB 211, MICB 201, SCIE 001

MICB 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
MICB 398.description: Work experience. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail.
MICB 398.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MICB_V 211, MICB_V 201 and one of MICB_V 212, MICB_V 202; or (b) BIOT_V 380

MICB 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
MICB 399.description: Work experience. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail.

MICB 401.title: Environmental Microbiology Laboratory
MICB 401.description: Microbiological analysis of environmental samples using culture-dependent and culture-independent methods.

MICB 402.title: Advanced Immunology
MICB 402.description: Molecular basis of lymphocyte development, activation and adhesion; immunogenetics and the major histocompatibility complex. Consult the credit exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the calendar.

children.raw: is used as the prerequisite for

MICB 402.prerequisiteText: One of MICB 302, BIOT 380. If MICB 302 is used as the prerequisite for MICB 402, students are required to take one of the following as a corequisite: BIOL 234, BIOL 335, MICB 325

MICB 404.title: Topics in Molecular Bacterial Pathogenesis
MICB 404.description: A lecture/discussion/library research course. Topics such as antibiotic resistance, pathogen genomics; host-pathogen interactions; evolution of pathogens; host responses to infection, invasive mechanisms, resistance mechanisms.
MICB 404.prerequisiteText: MICB 302 and one of MICB 308, MICB 408

MICB 405.title: Bioinformatics
MICB 405.description: Computational methods to analyze genome and protein sequences to derive structural and functional information. Related topics in functional genomics.
MICB 405.prerequisiteText: One of MICB 301, MICB 325, BIOC 302, BIOC 303, BIOL 335, BIOT 380

MICB 406.title: Topics in Molecular Virology
MICB 406.description: Presentations, library research, paper reviews, class discussions about current research in virology. Topics such as molecular targets in viral therapy; chronic viral infection; virus-host cell interaction.

MICB 407.title: Viral Infections in Humans.
MICB 407.description: Interactions between viruses and humans; pathogenesis; persistence and viral oncogenesis; virological diagnosis and treatment. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.)

MICB 408.title: Advanced Bacterial Pathogenesis
MICB 408.description: Current and emerging themes in bacterial pathogenesis including cellular microbiology, bacterial cell biology processes and their role in virulence including secretion systems to deliver virulence factors and immune evasion strategies employed by pathogens. Development of antibiotics and resistance to antibiotics.

MICB 412.title: Topics in Immunological Research
MICB 412.description: Presentations, library research, paper reviews and class discussion on selected areas of advanced molecular and cellular immunological research.

MICB 413.title: Topics in Microbiome Research
MICB 413.description: Critical examination and discussion of contemporary research literature concerning the impact of host-associated microbiomes on host development, health and disease with a focus on humans. Priority given to students in Microbiology and Immunology specializations.
MICB 413.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MICB 302 and one of MICB 308, MICB 325, BIOL 335; or (b) BIOT 380. And fourth-year standing in Science

MICB 418.title: Industrial Microbiology and Biotechnology
MICB 418.description: Exploitation of microbial and animal cells for the industrial production of chemicals ranging from alcohol to therapeutic proteins. Genetic manipulation of cellular characteristics, fermentation methods, patenting and governmental approval processes.

MICB 421.title: Experimental Microbiology
MICB 421.description: Research in microbial physiology and molecular genetics. Guided and independent laboratory projects are developed.

MICB 425.title: Microbial Ecological Genomics
MICB 425.description: Intrinsic and extrinsic forces driving prokaryotic genome evolution. Gene transfer; microbial species concepts; community genome structure, function and dynamics; ecological impacts of microbial genome diversity. Emphasis on problem solving and experimental design.

MICB 430.title: Seminar in Microbiological Literature
MICB 430.description: Student seminars on selected papers from the microbiological literature.

MICB 447.title: Experimental Molecular Biology
MICB 447.description: A laboratory course with a choice of independent, supervised research projects. Students develop protocols to carry out investigation of selected molecular biology problems.
MICB 447.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOT 380 or (b) MICB 323 or (c) all of MICB 322, MICB 398

MICB 448.title: Directed Research
MICB 448.description: A library (3 credits) or laboratory (3 or 6 credits) project. Requires permission of the Undergraduate Advisor. The results are presented in a written report to be reviewed by oral examination.
MICB 448.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MICB_V 323 or (b) all of MICB_V 322, MICB_V 399

MICB 449.title: Research Problem
MICB 449.description: A laboratory investigation in the final year of the Honours program. The results are presented in a written report, to be reviewed by oral examination.
MICB 449.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MICB 323 or (b) all of MICB 322, MICB 399

MICB 471.title: Laboratory Research in Microbiology and Immunology
MICB 471.description: A team-based laboratory research experience in microbiology and immunology.

MICB 475.title: Data Science Research in Microbiology and Immunology
MICB 475.description: A team-based data science research experience in microbiology and immunology.
MICB 475.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MICB 322 and one of MICB 325, BIOL 335; or (b) BIOT 380

MICB 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
MICB 498.description: Work experience. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail.

children.raw: completion of two co-op work terms

MICB 498.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MICB_V 399 or (b) BIOT_V 380. And completion of two co-op work terms

MICB 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
MICB 499.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during the Winter Session (Term 1) of fifth year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail.

MICB 502.title: Advanced Immunogenetics
MICB 502.description: Consult the Credit Exclusion List in the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.

MICB 506.title: Microbiological and Immunological Research
MICB 506.description: Developing, discussing, and undertaking research projects. Oral communication skills, peer review skills, scientific ethics, and the ability to critically evaluate papers in the literature.

MICB 507.title: Topics in Molecular Pathogenesis and Immunology

MICB 520.title: Topics in Microbiology, Immunology and Virology
MICB 520.description: Selected topics in a specific area within Microbiology, Immunology and Virology. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the department.

MICB 530.title: Student Seminars in Microbiology, Immunology and Virology
MICB 530.description: Student seminars on selected papers from the microbiology, immunology and virology literature.

MICB 548.title: Directed Studies on an Approved Problem

MICB 575.title: Data Science Research in Microbiology and Immunology
MICB 575.description: A team-based data science research experience in microbiology and immunology. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
